title: Clean bronze orders into a silver Delta table with PySpark
objective_text: Read a bronze table with PySpark, clean nulls, standardize types and write a silver Delta table.
scenario: The orders feed lands in bronze.orders as text. Finance's daily revenue report reads silver.orders and has been wrong twice this month: amounts with thousands separators went missing, half the dates didn't parse, and a retried load counted some orders twice. Build silver.orders so the report can trust it.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: A Delta table bronze.orders (13 rows, all text columns) in the exercise folder, and a starter answer.py.
required: order_id and customer_id are trimmed bigints.
order_date is a date read from order_ts, which comes as yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss or MM/dd/yyyy.
amount is decimal(10,2) with thousands commas removed; a blank amount is NULL.
status is trimmed and lower case; a blank status is 'unknown'.
Write silver.orders with columns order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status, so that running the code again leaves the same table.

expected.description: silver.orders has 10 rows, orders 1001 to 1010, each once, with no NULL order_id.

verifies: Your PySpark reads a bronze Delta table and writes a silver Delta table with the right types, keys and rows, on the exercise data and on rows you haven't seen, on this PC.
Running it again leaves the same table.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in a Databricks workspace, so it doesn't show Spark's own cast rules (ANSI mode), partitions or the table in Unity Catalog.
hints: Filter out rows with a NULL order_id first, so nothing later has to cope with them.
F.coalesce(F.to_date(col, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss'), F.to_date(col, 'MM/dd/yyyy')) takes whichever format parses.
Remove commas with F.regexp_replace before .cast('decimal(10,2)'), and turn a blank into NULL with F.when.
Trim before lower-casing status: ' Shipped ' and 'shipped' are the same status.
mode('overwrite') makes the write safe to repeat; append adds the rows again.
explanation: Filter the rows that can't be keyed, then standardize each column on the way to silver: trim and cast the ids, coalesce one to_date per format, strip separators and blank amounts before the decimal cast, trim and lower-case the status with a default, drop the exact duplicates by key, and overwrite the table so a rerun can't double it. The same steps in Spark SQL are a CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS SELECT (exercise E20).
troubleshooting: "Could not convert string" means a value reached a cast before it was cleaned: check the order of withColumn steps.
If order_date is NULL for some rows, one of the two formats isn't being parsed.
If the rerun check fails, the table is being appended to; overwrite it.
reset: Reset rebuilds bronze.orders from setup.sql, removes silver.orders and puts the starter back.
cleanup: Everything lives in this exercise's folder on this PC; Reset or removing the exercise deletes it. Nothing is created in any workspace.
